q: 1. *In orthographic projection, the projection's are always ........... to the plane of projection
explain: Orthographic projection is a system where the projectors are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 2. To emphasize the features on the side of an object the receding lines are drawn at the following angle to the plane of projection .............
explain: Drawing receding lines at an angle less than 45° reduces distortion on the side faces and helps emphasize/showcase the features on the side of the object in oblique projection.

q: 3. In oblique projections, a semi circle parallel to the plane of projection appears as .............
explain: Any plane figure that is parallel to the plane of projection in oblique projection is not foreshortened and hence retains its true shape — so a semicircle parallel to the plane still appears as a semicircle.

q: 4. *Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
explain: CAD software relies heavily on vector analysis and coordinate geometry to calculate positions and project 3D space onto a 2D screen.

q: 5. The projectors in oblique projections are .............
explain: In oblique projection, the parallel projectors strike the plane of projection at an angle other than 90°, i.e., they are inclined to the plane of projection (unlike orthographic projection where they are perpendicular).

q: 6. In the cavalier projection, an angle at which the projectors meet the plane of projection is .............
explain: Cavalier projection is characterized by receding lines drawn to full (true) scale with projectors typically inclined at 45° in most texts, but per this reference the projector angle is taken as 63°26'.

q: 7. When a line is perpendicular to a reference plane, its projection on the plane to which it is perpendicular is a:
explain: A line perpendicular to a plane is viewed 'end-on' from that plane, so its projection collapses to a single point.

q: 8. Presentation drawing are generally rendered due to
explain: Rendering in presentation drawings adds shadows, textures, and lighting to create a realistic effect for the viewer.

q: 9. The type of pictorial projection generally used by the architects is .............
explain: Architects commonly use perspective projection to present realistic, client-friendly visualizations of how a finished building will actually appear to an observer.

q: 10. Horizontal plane (HP) and vertical plane (VP) are always
explain: In the standard system of orthographic projection, HP and VP are set up perpendicular to each other, intersecting along the reference line (XY line).

q: 11. The most suitable angle for the cone of the vision for drawing perspective is
explain: In perspective drawing, a 30° to 60° cone of vision is considered standard to avoid distortion at the edges of the drawing.

q: 12. If the top view of a plane is a rhombus the object may be .............
explain: A rhombus-shaped top view can result from either a true rhombus lying flat, or a square viewed while inclined to the plane of projection (its edges foreshortening unevenly), so the object may be either a square or a rhombus.

q: 13. The trace of a hexagonal plane may be .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'an equilateral triangle' is marked as the answer for this item, reflecting a specific inclined orientation of the hexagonal plane considered in this reference.

q: 14. The projection obtained on a plane when the projectors converge to a point is known as
explain: Perspective projection uses projectors that converge at a single station point (the observer's eye), unlike parallel-projector methods.

q: 15. The length of the rectangle representing the development of the lateral surface of a right circular cylinder is equal to :
options: twice the circumference of circular base
explain: When a cylinder is 'unrolled,' the length of the resulting rectangle is the distance around the circle, which is the circumference ($2\pi r$).

q: 16. If both the principle views of a plane object are ellipse of the same size, the side view will be .............
explain: When both front and top views appear as equal-sized ellipses, the plane is inclined to both HP and VP; consequently its side view (edge view) appears as an inclined straight line.

q: 17. Third angle projection is the traditional ........... system.
explain: Third-angle projection is primarily used in the United States and Canada, whereas Europe and Asia typically use First-angle.

q: 18. Among the following solids, a regular polyhedron is .............
explain: A regular polyhedron has all faces as identical regular polygons meeting in the same way at each vertex; among the given options, only the cube (all faces equal squares) satisfies this, while a sphere is not a polyhedron at all.

q: 19. The projection in which the length, breadth and height of an object is shown in one view is Known as :
explain: Isometric projection is a type of pictorial projection that shows all three dimensions in a single view at specific angles.

q: 20. The shades and shadows are :
options: the result of object on the ground
the result of light on the ground
explain: Shades refer to the dark parts on the object itself, while shadows are the dark areas cast by the object onto another surface.

q: 21. The face of an object containing circles, irregular shapes, etc. is kept parallel to the plane of projection is known as .............
explain: In oblique projection, the face with circular or irregular details is deliberately kept parallel to the plane of projection so it can be drawn true to shape without distortion, while other faces recede at an angle.

q: 22. The base angles used for drawing an isometric projection are:
explain: Isometric drawing uses one vertical (0° from vertical) axis and two receding axes drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

q: 23. The curve of intersection of a vertical cone with an auxiliary vertical plane is .............
explain: An auxiliary vertical plane cutting a cone parallel to one of its generators (slant lines) produces a parabolic section, as per the conic section relationships.

q: 24. Select the incorrect statement about orthographic projections :
options: the reference planes are also called the principle planes
the object must the situated in the first quadrant
the planes of projection and assumed to be transparent
projections are obtained by drawing perpendicular s from the object to the planes
explain: While the planes are assumed transparent in 3rd angle, the statement is contextually marked incorrect based on general principle definitions in the key.

q: 25. When a line is perpendicular to a reference plane, its projection on the plane to which it is perpendicular is .............
explain: A line perpendicular to a plane projects onto that plane as a single point, since the entire length of the line collapses to one location when viewed along its own axis.

q: 26. In the first angle method of orthographic projection
options: the object comes between the observer and the plane
the plane comes between the object and the observer
the observer comes between the object and the plane
explain: In first-angle projection, the sequence is Observer -> Object -> Plane.

q: 27. Horizontal plane and vertical plane are always .............
explain: By definition in orthographic projection theory, the Horizontal Plane (HP) and Vertical Plane (VP) are mutually perpendicular reference planes.

q: 28. Isometric projection is:
options: an orthographic projection of pictorial type
explain: Isometric projection is technically a form of orthographic (pictorial) projection, and is also commonly grouped among pictorial/oblique-type projections used in drafting.

q: 29. Isometric projection of a sphere is a circle having a diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'less than that of sphere' is marked correct here; this corresponds to isometric projection drawn using the true (reduced) isometric scale (~0.816), giving a projected circle smaller than the sphere's actual diameter.

q: 30. The angle between isometric axes is .............
explain: The three isometric axes are conventionally arranged at 120° to one another, giving the standard isometric drawing its characteristic symmetric appearance.

q: 31. Most suitable hand drawn coloured perspective drawing paper is:
explain: Any good quality coloured paper is considered suitable for hand-drawn coloured perspective presentation drawings.

q: 32. In isometric projection, circles are represented as ellipse on .............
explain: Since every face of an isometric drawing is inclined to the viewing direction, circles on any face (front, top, or side) are represented as ellipses in isometric projection.

q: 33. In general structural drawings would typically include following information:
explain: Structural drawings are comprehensive and include orientation (North), geometric views, and material specifications.

q: 34. Oblique projection are of:
explain: Oblique projection (cavalier/cabinet) is commonly drawn with the receding axis at either 45° or 30° to the horizontal.

q: 35. *A technical drawing of an object that shows the relationship or order of assembly of the various parts is known
explain: An exploded view drawing shows the components of an object separated but in their correct relative positions for assembly.

q: 36. In isometric projection, dimension lines are drawn .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'none of these' is marked correct; conventionally, dimension lines in isometric drawings are drawn parallel to the respective isometric axes, but the given key selects option (d) for this item.

q: 37. The point of intersection of co-ordinate axis is called .............
explain: The point where the coordinate axes (X, Y, Z) intersect, representing the reference point (0,0,0), is universally called the origin.

q: 38. In 1st angle projection the right side view must be drawn on .... side of the FV:
explain: In first angle projection each view is placed on the side opposite to the direction it is viewed from, so the right side view appears to the left of the front view.

q: 39. When the receding lines are drawn to full size scale then the oblique projection is
explain: In Cavalier projection, the receding (depth) axis is drawn at its full actual length.

q: 40. Perspective drawing are mostly used in drawing:
options: elevation of proposed building, exhibition stalls bridges etc.
side view of proposed building, exhibition stalls bridges etc.
explain: As given by the answer key, none of the specific listed options is the standard answer; perspective drawings are generally used for realistic presentation views rather than technical plans/elevations.

q: 41. When the receding lines are drawn to half size scale then the oblique projection is
explain: In Cabinet projection, the receding axis is reduced by half to create a more realistic appearance to the human eye.

q: 42. The angle that isometric lines make with each other is .............
explain: The isometric lines (edges parallel to the isometric axes) are mutually inclined at 120° to each other, giving the standard isometric drawing its symmetric triangular appearance.

q: 43. A square in a regular multi-view projection appears in an isometric view as .............
explain: A square face, when drawn in isometric view (inclined to the viewer along isometric axes), is foreshortened into a rhombus shape.

q: 44. The illusion of depth in paintings is depicting by .............
explain: Aerial (atmospheric) perspective creates the illusion of depth in paintings through variations in color, tone, and clarity (distant objects appearing hazier/lighter), as distinct from linear (vanishing-point) perspective methods.

q: 45. The number of stages that are necessary to get the orthographic views of a solid having its axis inclined to both the reference planes .............
explain: When a solid's axis is inclined to both HP and VP, obtaining its true orthographic views requires a sequence of three stages: drawing it in simple position, tilting the axis to the given inclination with one plane, then further changing position relative to the other plane.

q: 46. A tetrahedron is resting on its face on the HP with a side perpendicular to the VP. Its front view will be .............
explain: With a tetrahedron resting on a triangular face on HP and one edge perpendicular to VP, the front view (projected along the direction perpendicular to VP) appears as an isosceles triangle due to the way the base edge foreshortens.

q: 47. A square pyramid is resting on a face in the VP. The number of dotted lines that will appear in the front view .............
explain: With the square pyramid resting on a triangular face against VP, the hidden (invisible) edges behind the visible face project as two dotted (hidden) lines in the front view.

q: 48. The elevation is a:
explain: An elevation can refer to the front, back, or side view of an object depending on which vertical face is being projected.

q: 49. The method by which the development of surface of an oblique solid is obtained .............
explain: Since an oblique solid's surface lacks the regular symmetry needed for exact radial-line or parallel-line development, its development is obtained approximately, using the approximation method.

q: 50. Methods for the development of solids are .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'triangular method' is marked as the sole correct answer, though in general practice, parallel-line, radial-line, and triangulation methods are all standard techniques for surface development of solids.
